subject: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.dev>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clockwork.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.dev>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I wanted to put our starting point in writing so your procurement and finance teams have the shape of the offer to review. Key pieces below:

- Proposed commit: $75k/month (hosted API) with per-token billing and an anticipated steady-state of ~250M tokens/month after ramp.
- Ladder breakpoints (marginal pricing):
  - 0 - 100M tokens: $0.0060/token
  - 100M - 300M tokens: $0.0048/token
  - 300M+: $0.0036/token
- Option A (marginal): you pay the marginal rate for tokens in each band (recommended for simplicity).
- Option B (blended true-up): we calculate an effective blended rate each month and apply a true-up against the committed spend (adds accounting/administration but yields a predictable invoice).
- Clawback/true-up mechanics: monthly reconciliation with a quarterly true-up cap (we can cap clawback to 20% of committed spend per quarter as a concession).

I attached the pricing model workbook and a one-page summary for internal review. Can you share a sense of which approach (marginal vs blended) your finance team prefers and whether the quarterly cap on clawback is acceptable? If helpful we can run a scenario with your actual monthly token profile to show invoice outcomes.

Next step: if procurement likes the shape, I can send a draft SOW + DocuSign link for signature and route to our Legal for the limited clawback language.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.dev | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Model_Q3_v2.xlsx (xls xlsx), pricing_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clockwork.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.dev>
Cc: procurement@clockwork.health
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 11:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics

Kim —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick items from our side:

1) Finance prefers the blended true-up model for predictability on the P&L.
2) Procurement is worried about large month-to-month swings during our pilot (we expect a burst month at launch then lower steady-state). Can the quarterly cap be reduced to 15%?
3) We will need to see sample invoices for both approaches (marginal vs blended) across three ramp scenarios so we understand cash flow impact.

I'll loop in the rest of procurement if we move forward, but for now please send the sample invoices/scenarios.

—Sarah
Sarah Miller
Head of Product Ops, Clockwork Health
sarah.miller@clockwork.health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.dev>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.dev>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics

Folks — forwarding Sarah's ask. Procurement wants blended true-up and a tighter quarterly clawback cap (15%). They also want sample invoices for three ramp scenarios (slow, expected, burst). Can you run the model and prepare a one-page comparison (marginal vs blended) plus sample invoice PDFs we can send back?

We should show
- monthly invoice amounts for each scenario over a 6-month horizon
- effective blended rate under Option B per month
- cash-flow impact (largest single-month invoice)

Ben, please include a version that keeps the 20% cap and one with 15% so we can offer both. Neha, FYI in case Legal/Finance needs specific language for the cap.

Thanks —
Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.dev>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.dev>
Date: Mon, 7 May 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics

Kim —

Attached is a short deliverable: pricing_summary.pdf (one-pager), plus a three-scenario workbook (Redwood_Pricing_Model_Q3_v2.xlsx) that includes the comparisons you requested. Highlights from the runs:

- Under the "burst" scenario, marginal billing yields a peak invoice 28% higher than the blended true-up monthly invoice for the same token count.
- Moving the quarterly clawback cap from 20% to 15% reduces Redwood's downside protection by ~1.7 percentage points on gross margin across the 6-month window (roughly $8.6k on the modeled commit).
- For Clockwork's expected ramp, blended true-up stabilizes month-to-month invoices and the effective blended rate converges within 10% of the marginal-weighted rate by month 3.

I've left comments in the workbook on the exact math and included an example invoice PDF (sample_invoice_burst.pdf) that uses the blended approach.

If you want formal language for the 15% cap, I can draft a short clause; Legal may push back but we can offer a stepped-clawback that starts at 20% for quarter 1 and steps to 15% starting quarter 2 as a compromise.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Pricing & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.dev

Attachments: pricing_summary.pdf, sample_invoice_burst.pdf, Redwood_Pricing_Model_Q3_v2.xlsx

Subject: Re: Per-token ladder: smoothing proposal & true-up mechanics

Sarah —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are three scenario invoices and a one-page comparison that shows marginal vs blended outcomes, plus two clawback options:

A) Quarterly clawback cap 20% (standard)
B) Stepped concession — 20% Q1, 15% Q2+ (Redwood proposed compromise)

We recommend Option B for Clockwork to reduce risk at launch while preserving a modest protection for Redwood. If that looks good, we can incorporate the stepped cap into the SOW and route for signature. DocuSign link below will be enabled once Legal signs off on the collar language.

Kim —

Thanks — the materials are clear and the stepped concession (20% then 15%) is acceptable to procurement as a path forward. Finance still prefers the blended true-up; procurement is OK with the stepped cap.

Please send the SOW with the stepped clawback clause and we'll circulate internally for signature. I expect a final yes next week after procurement signs off.

—Sarah

P.S. If Legal has sample language, please include it in the SOW so we can avoid back-and-forth redlines on the clawback numeric.
